beats.say: Fold one sheet of paper a hundred and three times, and it's thicker than the universe is wide.
One sheet is a tenth of a millimeter. Every fold doubles it. Seven folds: twelve point eight millimeters.
Fold twenty seven: over thirteen kilometers. You just passed Mount Everest.
Fold thirty two: you're above the space station.
Fold forty two: about four hundred and forty thousand kilometers. That is past the Moon.
Fold fifty one: past the Sun.
Fold sixty nine: past the nearest star.
Fold eighty eight: out of our galaxy and past Andromeda.
Fold one hundred and three: a hundred and seven billion light years. The observable universe is ninety three.
The real world record? Twelve folds. Britney Gallivan did it in 2001, with over a kilometer of tissue paper.
beats.speak: The real world record? Twelve folds. Britney Gallivan did it in two thousand and one, with over a kilometer of tissue paper.

title: How many folds to make paper thicker than the universe?
caption: A sheet of paper is about 0.1 mm thick and every fold doubles it. 7 folds: 12.8 mm. 27 folds: 13.4 km, taller than Everest (8,848.86 m). 32 folds: above the space station (about 250 miles up). 42 folds: 439,805 km, past the Moon (384,400 km). 51 folds: past the Sun. 69: past Proxima Centauri. 88: past Andromeda (2.5 million light-years). 103 folds: about 107 billion light-years, wider than the observable universe (about 93 billion light-years). The real record is 12 folds, set by Britney Gallivan in 2001 with 1,219 m of tissue paper. That's exponential growth: 2 to the power of 103.
